topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn about cancer causation.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations can give rise to cancer through clonal evolution within a susceptible biological setting.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposure to cancer risk despite individual variation and uncertainty about causation.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example.

topics.label: Environmental exposures and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations through their interactions with cellular processes.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish initiating mutations from the promoter activity that enables mutated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Biological context and carcinogen specificity
topics.groupedBecause: The discussion of developmental susceptibility culminates in a recap of how carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context of exposure.

topics.label: Human evidence linking exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence from human samples and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results do not fully reproduce human cancer development.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risk and the difficulty of assessing carcinogenic hazards.
